summary: A rare opening that states how the economy moved: growth or jobs up, credited to the people or Congress.
realLife: Reagan in 1986 credited the people with many straight months of growth early on; Clinton in 1999 opened on jobs, wages, a balanced budget and a surplus, all up. The other four addresses read gave no national figure in the first paragraph.
sources: Read Nov 24, 2026: the first and last paragraphs of each address on the Presidency Project page; the middles were not read.
inGame: The macro-month records give run-good, run-pay-ahead and run-jobs-gained facts and a span (`run-span`); said in words, never as figures. The game's `report` lines for the State of the Union use them.

turns.what: The same figures read as a loss: jobs and pay down.
turns.writesBack: The paper opens on the loss; the housemate may blame the speaker.

turns.what: The figure is named without a direction.
turns.writesBack: The listener asks which way (the pre-grade's figure rule).
